questions.q: Match each feature of good governance with its correct meaning.

pairs.r: Government decisions are open and accessible
Everyone is equal before the law
Public officials are responsible for their actions

questions.explanation: These are five of the seven features of good governance shown in the chapter; the remaining two are effectiveness (public resources are used wisely) and inclusiveness (every citizen has equal opportunities).
questions.fact: Features of good governance include responsiveness, transparency, participation, the rule of law, accountability, effectiveness, and inclusiveness.
questions.hint: Match the keyword in each feature to what it protects.

questions.q: Which feature of good governance is reflected when public resources are used wisely?
options: Responsiveness
Inclusiveness
Transparency
Effectiveness
questions.explanation: Effectiveness means that public resources are used wisely. This ensures that the money and materials belonging to the public actually produce the intended results.
questions.fact: Effectiveness: Public resources are used wisely.
questions.hint: The name itself suggests producing results.

questions.q: Governance is the government's responsibility, but good governance depends on how different sections of society and government perform their responsibilities and work with one another.
questions.explanation: The government makes laws and policies, but citizens, media, civil society, and the private sector must also do their part. When all perform their responsibilities honestly and work together, governance becomes effective and public welfare is achieved.
questions.fact: Governance is the government's responsibility, but good governance depends on how different sections of society and government perform their responsibilities and work with one another.
questions.hint: Good governance is a team effort.

questions.q: The features of good governance include responsiveness, transparency, participation, the rule of law, accountability, effectiveness, and ___.
questions.explanation: The seventh feature is inclusiveness, which means every citizen has equal opportunities. Together these features ensure that public institutions serve the people effectively.
questions.fact: Features of good governance include responsiveness, transparency, participation, the rule of law, accountability, effectiveness, and inclusiveness.
questions.hint: This word comes from 'including everyone'.

questions.q: Match each actor with the role it plays in society, as described in the chapter.

pairs.r: Makes laws and policies and provides public services
Elect their representatives, follow the law, and participate in public life
Helps people understand public issues and brings important matters to public attention
Work with communities and raise awareness about social concerns
Contributes through economic activity and innovation

questions.explanation: Each section of society has a distinct responsibility, and good governance emerges when all of them perform their duties and cooperate with one another.
questions.fact: The government makes laws and policies and provides public services. Citizens elect their representatives, follow the law, and participate in public life. The media helps people understand public issues. Civil society organisations work with communities. The private sector contributes through economic activity and innovation.
questions.hint: Think about who does what in daily public life.

questions.q: Select all correct effects of governance mentioned in the chapter.
options: It helps maintain law and order
It keeps citizens away from public life
It protects the rights and freedom of citizens
It helps people access public services like education and healthcare
questions.explanation: Governance maintains law and order so that people can live safely and peacefully, protects rights and freedoms, and helps people access public services such as education, healthcare, and transport. It never keeps citizens away from public life — participation is at its heart.
questions.fact: It helps maintain law and order... It protects the rights and freedom of citizens... It also helps people access important public services, such as education, healthcare, transport.
questions.hint: Three of these build citizens' lives; one does the opposite.

questions.q: On which date is National Good Governance Day celebrated?
options: 25th December
26th January
15th August
2nd October
questions.explanation: 25th December is celebrated as National Good Governance Day. It reminds us of the commitment needed from institutions and citizens for good governance.
questions.fact: 25th December is celebrated as National Good Governance Day.
questions.hint: It is the same date as Christmas.

questions.q: Select all challenges to good governance mentioned in the chapter.
options: Weak coordination between institutions and departments
Regular monitoring of programmes
Unequal access to public services
Misinformation and fake news
questions.explanation: Weak coordination affects the implementation of government programmes, unequal access leaves some groups or communities behind, and misinformation and fake news mislead people. Regular monitoring, by contrast, is a solution, not a challenge.
questions.fact: Weak coordination between different institutions and departments can affect the implementation of government programmes... Unequal access to public services can leave some groups or communities behind... Misinformation and fake news also pose a serious challenge to good governance.
questions.hint: Monitoring is a remedy, not a problem.

questions.q: Malpractices and misuse of public offices can prevent resources and benefits from reaching the people.
questions.explanation: Malpractices and misuse of public offices divert resources away from the people. Addressing such challenges requires effective institutions, responsible officials, and active citizens.
questions.fact: Malpractices and misuse of public offices can prevent resources and benefits from reaching the people.
questions.hint: Corruption blocks the path of public benefits.

questions.q: What is e-governance?
options: The use of information and communication technology by governments to provide public services
Selling government offices to private companies
Holding elections through newspapers
Printing more paper files in offices
questions.explanation: E-governance is the use of information and communication technology (ICT) by governments to provide public services, share information, communicate with citizens, receive feedback, and improve administrative processes.
questions.fact: E-governance refers to the use of information and communication technology by governments to provide public services, share information, communicate with citizens, receive feedback, and improve administrative processes.
questions.hint: The 'e' stands for electronic.

questions.q: Governance does not affect the daily life of ordinary citizens.
questions.explanation: Governance affects many aspects of our daily life — from law and order to education, healthcare, and transport. The roads, water, parks, and electricity we use every day all depend on it.
questions.fact: Governance affects many aspects of our daily life.
questions.hint: Think of the roads, water, and schools you use daily.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): E-governance can make governance more transparent, accessible, and convenient for citizens.
Reason (R): E-governance substantially reduces paperwork and allows people to access services without visiting government offices.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true: the chapter says e-governance makes governance more transparent, accessible, convenient and quick, and this is possible because it reduces paperwork and removes the need to visit offices. So R explains A.
questions.fact: It can make governance more transparent, accessible, and convenient and quick for the citizens. E-governance substantially reduces paperwork and allows people to access services without visiting government offices.
questions.hint: Ask whether the reason is the cause of the assertion.

questions.q: Select all options that are e-governance initiatives named in the chapter.
options: DigiLocker
PM POSHAN
Aadhaar
CPGRAMS
questions.explanation: UMANG, Aadhaar, GeM (Government e-Marketplace), DigiLocker, CPGRAMS, and APAAR are the e-governance initiatives listed in the chapter. PM POSHAN, by contrast, is mentioned as a public policy, not an e-governance platform.
questions.fact: The chapter lists e-governance initiatives: UMANG, Aadhaar, GeM (Government e-Marketplace), DigiLocker, CPGRAMS, and APAAR.
questions.hint: Three of these are digital platforms for government services.

questions.q: E-governance is particularly valuable in a large country like India because it helps deliver public services across vast geographical areas.
questions.explanation: In a large country like India, e-governance enables governments to deliver public services efficiently, transparently, conveniently, and quickly to citizens across vast geographical areas.
questions.fact: E-governance is particularly valuable in a large country like India, as it enables governments to deliver public services more efficiently, transparently, conveniently, and quickly to citizens across vast geographical areas.
questions.hint: Distance matters less when services go digital.

questions.q: Which of these statements about e-governance is INCORRECT?
options: Digital technology has changed the way the government interacts with people
E-governance is only effective when people have access to digital devices, reliable internet, and the skills to use them
The government must ensure that digital services remain inclusive and accessible to everyone
E-governance benefits every citizen equally, regardless of their access to devices or the internet
questions.explanation: The chapter warns that e-governance is only effective when people have access to digital devices, reliable internet, and the skills to use them. Without inclusive access many citizens can be left out, so the government must keep digital services accessible to all.
questions.fact: E-governance is only effective when people have access to digital devices, reliable internet, and the skills needed to use them... the government must also ensure that digital services remain inclusive and accessible to everyone.
questions.hint: Think about people who have no smartphone or internet.

questions.q: The roads we travel on, the clean drinking water supplied to our homes, and the public parks where we play are all examples of ___.
options: private business activities
public services made possible through public policies
natural gifts that need no management
personal family property
questions.explanation: Such everyday services are made possible through public policies, which help make our daily lives safer, healthier, and more convenient. We experience the impact of public policies often without even noticing it.
questions.fact: The roads we travel on, the clean drinking water supplied to our homes, the electricity that lights our classrooms, the public parks where we play, and the waste collected from our neighbourhood are all examples of public services made possible through public policies.
questions.hint: Who provides and maintains these things for everyone?

questions.q: In the school example, why do the decisions of the 'Plastic-Free Campus Policy' form a policy?
options: Because the principal ordered them without any discussion
Because they provide a planned course of action to solve a problem and achieve a sustainable goal
Because they punish all the students
Because they were copied from another school
questions.explanation: The decisions form a policy because they provide a planned course of action to solve the plastic-waste problem and achieve a sustainable goal. The principal first discussed the issue with teachers, students, and parents.
questions.fact: These decisions form a policy because they provide a planned course of action to solve a problem and achieve a sustainable goal.
questions.hint: A policy is a plan of action, not a random order.

questions.q: According to the chapter, what is public policy?
options: A course of action adopted by the government to solve public problems and promote the welfare of society
A rule made only for government employees
A decision taken by private companies to increase their profits
A tradition followed by one family
questions.explanation: Public policy is a course of action adopted by the government to solve public problems, meet people's needs, and promote the welfare of society. It is monitored and evaluated through a feedback loop and changed if required.
questions.fact: Public policy is a result of a course of action adopted by the government to solve public problems, meet people's needs, and promote the welfare of society.
questions.hint: Focus on the word 'public' — the whole society.

questions.q: The word 'public' refers to all the people living in a ___ or community.
questions.explanation: 'Public' means all the people living in a society or community. A policy becomes a public policy when it is made for the public benefit, implemented by public institutions, and often financed with public money.
questions.fact: The word 'public' refers to all the people living in a society or community.
questions.hint: It is the opposite of 'private'.

questions.q: A company allows its employees to work from home twice a week. Why is this a policy but NOT a public policy?
options: Because it saves the company money
Because it applies only to a particular organisation or a limited group of people
Because it is not written down anywhere
Because the government disapproves of it
questions.explanation: Schools, companies, hospitals, sports clubs, and families may have their own policies, but these apply only to a particular organisation or a limited group. Public policies are formulated by governments to address issues that affect society on a larger scale.
questions.fact: These policies apply only to a particular organisation or a limited group of people. Public policies, on the other hand, are formulated by governments to address issues that affect society on a larger scale.
questions.hint: Who does the rule cover — everyone or just some?

questions.q: Select all conditions under which a policy becomes a public policy.
options: It is made for the public benefit
It applies only to the staff of one private company
It is implemented by public institutions
It is often financed with public money collected through taxes
questions.explanation: A policy becomes public when it is made for the public benefit, implemented by public institutions, and often financed with public money collected through taxes. A rule limited to one company's staff remains a private policy.
questions.fact: A policy becomes public policy when it is made for the public benefit, implemented by public institutions, and often financed with public money collected through taxes.
questions.hint: Ask who benefits, who implements, and who pays.

questions.q: According to the chapter, how do people help shape public policies?
options: Only by voting once in five years
By identifying issues, expressing concerns, participating in consultations, and sharing feedback
By avoiding all public discussions
By leaving every decision entirely to experts
questions.explanation: People identify issues, express their concerns, participate in consultations, provide suggestions, and share feedback after a policy is implemented. Governments use this feedback to improve policies over time.
questions.fact: People identify issues, express their concerns, participate in consultations, provide suggestions, and share feedback after a policy is implemented.
questions.hint: Their role continues before, during, and after a policy.

questions.q: Which organisation assists countries in controlling infectious diseases, as the chapter's example of international organisations' role in policy-making?
options: The World Health Organization (WHO)
The World Trade Organization (WTO)
A national cricket board
A local residents' welfare association
questions.explanation: International organisations bring in international experience, technical know-how, and financial support. The WHO assisting countries in controlling infectious diseases is the chapter's example of this role.
questions.fact: The World Health Organization (WHO) assists countries in controlling infectious diseases.
questions.hint: Its name tells you it deals with health worldwide.

questions.q: Public policies deal only with issues that concern one private organisation, not society as a whole.
questions.explanation: Public policies address issues that concern society as a whole, such as education, healthcare, transportation, sanitation, environmental protection, and public safety. Policies of one private organisation are not public policies.
questions.fact: Public policies address issues that concern society as a whole, such as education, healthcare, transportation, sanitation, environmental protection, and public safety.
questions.hint: The word 'public' points to society at large.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Public policy translates governance into planned action.
Reason (R): Public policy turns public concerns and government priorities into programmes, decisions, and solutions.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true: governance needs concrete instruments to address public problems, and public policy provides that link by turning concerns and priorities into programmes, decisions, and solutions. Hence R explains A.
questions.fact: Public policy... translates governance into planned action by turning public concerns and government priorities into programmes, decisions, and solutions.
questions.hint: Policy is the bridge between ideas and action.
